passages.original: Ταῦθ’ ἱστορεῖ ὁ Καισαρεὺς Εὐσέβιος ὁ Παμφίλου ν τῷ λόγῳ ὃς ἐκλήθη Βασιλικός. Ἀρχὴ κόσμου.
passages.english: These things are recounted by Eusebius of Caesarea, [the son] of Pamphilus, in the discourse which was called the Basilikos. Beginning of the world.
passages.notes: The stray "ν" before τῷ is taken as a scanning error for ἐν ("in"). "Basilikos" ("Royal [Oration]") presumably refers to Eusebius' oration in praise of Constantine. "Of Pamphilus" is Eusebius' usual epithet, after his teacher Pamphilus. The Greek is simply the genitive, so "[the son]" follows the conventional rendering.
